conclusions: User confirmation proves the observed Mac-created project A7 byte represents U+00DF sharp-s, consistent with MacRoman for that specimen.
The current native Mac PMR filename converter is not hardcoded to MacRoman. It passes selector5 into shared conversion helpers, which call CFStringGetSystemEncoding.
The same library has an explicit fixedMacRoman selector1; PMR current-Mac wrappers use selector5 instead.
Native PMR Project is a counted legacy byte string in both sets; ReadString/WriteString do not encode/transcode it or attach a codepage tag.

One traced Project producer path obtains _PJ/PROJNAME through CoreAttrList::FindString. UTF8 attribute kind4 is converted to current Mac system encoding; legacy string kind2 is copied without transcoding. Those bytes are cached and written unchanged to PMR.

filenameReadChain.operation: CurrentMacMBCSEncodingToUnicodeString passes ScriptEncoding selector5 to EncodedToUTF16
EncodedToUTF16 uses fixed table only for selectors1..3, otherwise calls CFStringGetSystemEncoding
CFStringCreateWithBytes consumes bytes under returned encoding

filenameWriteChain.operation: Pass returned encoding to CFStringRefToEncoded; output uses CFStringGetBytes

projectChain.operation: CMGetProjectName queries _PJ via AAttrList FindString; PROJNAME fallback at0x282bfc..0x282c1c
AAttrList FindString delegates to CoreAttrList FindString
CoreAttrList FindString branches on attribute kind2/4. Kind2 calls FindStringOnly; kind4 reads UTF8 then calls UTF8ToCurrentMacMBCSEncoding
FindStringOnly copies legacy kind2 bytes via strncpy and terminates
Copy project to buffer and pass buffer x5 through cache operation virtual+0x328
AddCacheEntry copies/interns project bytes; empty project can use current project name
INFO2REC retrieves interned project and strcpy to record+0x240
WritePmrRec writes project via WriteString in v16 and legacy branches
WriteString writes uint16 strlen then bytes, with no encoding conversion or tag

sdk.CFStringGetSystemEncodingComment: The default encoding for the system; untagged 8-bit characters are usually in this encoding

otherEncodingPathsNotToConfuse: DefaultCodePage0x34170 calls GetApplicationTextEncoding then GetTextEncodingBase and caches it. This was not the conversion path invoked by the traced PMR currentMac helpers.

StringEncodingConversions initializer0x12dde8 calls GetApplicationTextEncoding and stores result at0x3e030c, but traced selector5 helpers directly call CFStringGetSystemEncoding rather than reading that global.
limits: Only installed Mac arm64 Media Composer26.8.0.58987 examined here; no Windows binary or historical release inspected.
No codepage tag identified in PMR framing or fields. CF system encoding can require external runtime/system knowledge.
Project kind2 pass-through can preserve bytes from an earlier producer; current writer does not normalize every existing legacy value.
The current machine CF encoding and official Apple function semantics are being independently researched by parent; not inferred only from function names.
No claim that every historical PMR is MacRoman follows from these native paths.

sources.title: Avid Unity MediaNetwork File Manager Setup Guide
sources.retrieval: Full PDF opened; international character support pages inspected.
sources.claim: For MediaNetwork3.1 and earlier, European-language filenames created by Avid Composer Products on both Macintosh and Windows used MacRoman. Asian-language Avid clients after installing a language kit used Windows-native language encoding, such as ANSI Japanese. Later MediaNetwork stores Unicode and clients transcode according to platform.
sources.limit: File Manager filename behavior and history, not a declaration of the exact PMR Project field. It is direct evidence that Avid legacy text is not universally Roman across all locales.

conclusions: MacRoman is the established decoding for the observed Mac-created project pattern and documented Roman Avid naming convention.
Current native Mac PMR conversion asks CFStringGetSystemEncoding; it does not select the library fixedMacRoman selector.
The standalone public API probe on this machine returned encoding0 Western (Mac OS Roman) and decoded A7 as U+00DF.
Project Unicode-to-legacy conversion follows the system codec, while already-legacy attributes can pass through unchanged. Both PMR sets store the same Project bytes.
A universal all-platform/all-locale MacRoman PMR schema is not established; official Avid sources describe locale-specific exceptions.
No production source or media was changed; web source text was not executed.
